turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Your resume looks good, but frankly, many candidates are qualified. Convince me—what are the three main reasons I should hire you over someone else?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There are three reasons. First, I've already done this job: two years running the help desk on my campus. Second, I learn tools fast, I picked up your CRM over a weekend just for this interview.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Third, I stay calm with upset customers. My satisfaction score was four point eight out of five. So, experience, speed, and calm.

transcript: There are three reasons. First, I've already done this job: two years running the help desk on my campus. Second, I learn tools fast, I picked up your CRM over a weekend just for this interview. Third, I stay calm with upset customers. My satisfaction score was four point eight out of five. So, experience, speed, and calm.

rubric.check: Gives exactly three distinct reasons or points (not two, not four or more)
The three reasons are clearly separated so a listener could count them
Each reason clearly supports the one case they are making

why: Previews the count, signposts each reason, sums up; split across two turns.
